arxiv-2007-04911.title: GAMA: a General Automated Machine learning Assistant
arxiv-2007-04911.creator: Pieter Gijsbers[✉], Joaquin Vanschoren
arxiv-2007-04911.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Pieter Gijsbers[✉], Joaquin Vanschoren. The General Automated Machine learning Assistant (GAMA) is a modular AutoML system developed to empower users to track and control how AutoML algorithms search for optimal machine learning pipelines, and facilitate AutoML research itself. In contrast to current, often black-box systems, GAMA allows users to plug in different AutoML and post-processing techniques, logs and visualizes the search process, and supports easy benchmarking.

arxiv-2206-02257.title: Efficient Annotation and Learning for 3D Hand Pose Estimation: A Survey
arxiv-2206-02257.creator: Takehiko Ohkawa, Ryosuke Furuta, Yoichi Sato
arxiv-2206-02257.description: Abstract In this survey, we present a systematic review of 3D hand pose estimation from the perspective of efficient annotation and learning. 3D hand pose estimation has been an important research area owing to its potential to enable various applications, such as video understanding, AR/VR, and robotics.

arxiv-2211-16605.title: Top-Down Synthesis for Library Learning DOI: 10.1145/3571234 popl23main-p278-p Journal: PACMPL Volume: 7 POPL 41 1 CCS: Software and its engineering Automatic programming
arxiv-2211-16605.creator: Matthew Bowers, Theo X. Olausson, Lionel Wong, Gabriel Grand, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Kevin Ellis, Armando Solar-Lezama
arxiv-2211-16605.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Matthew Bowers, Theo X. Olausson, Lionel Wong, Gabriel Grand, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Kevin Ellis, Armando Solar-Lezama. This paper introduces corpus-guided top-down synthesis as a mechanism for synthesizing library functions that capture common functionality from a corpus of programs in a domain specific language (DSL). The algorithm builds abstractions directly from initial DSL primitives, using syntactic pattern matching of intermediate abstractions to intelligently prune the search space and guide the algorithm towards abstractions that maximally capture shared structures in the corpus.

arxiv-2305-05113.title: Object-Centric Alignments
arxiv-2305-05113.creator: Lukas Liss, Jan Niklas Adams, Wil M.P. van der Aalst
arxiv-2305-05113.description: Abstract Processes tend to interact with other processes and operate on various objects of different types. These objects can influence each other creating dependencies between sub-processes. Analyzing the conformance of such complex processes challenges traditional conformance-checking approaches because they assume a single-case identifier for a process. To create a single-case identifier one has to flatten complex processes.

arxiv-2310-10805.title: Global stabilization of the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the torus
arxiv-2310-10805.creator: Kévin Le Balc’h, Jérémy Martin
arxiv-2310-10805.description: Abstract In this article, we prove the (uniform) global exponential stabilization of the cubic defocusing Schrödinger equation on the torus ( ℝ / 2 ​ π ​ ℤ ) d (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^{d} , for d = 1 d=1 , 2 2 or 3 3 , with a linear damping localized in a subset of the torus satisfying some geometrical assumptions.

arxiv-2409-07512.title: Variational wavefunction for Mott insulator at finite U U using ancilla qubits
arxiv-2409-07512.creator: Boran Zhou, Hui-Ke Jin, Ya-Hui Zhang
arxiv-2409-07512.description: Abstract The Mott regime with finite U U offers a promising platform for exploring novel phases of matter, such as quantum spin liquids (QSL) that exhibit fractionalization and emergent gauge field. Here, we provide a new class wavefunction, dubbed ancilla wavefunction, to capture both charge and spin (gauge) fluctuations in QSLs at finite U U .

arxiv-2504-05288.title: Seeking and Updating with Live Visual Knowledge
arxiv-2504-05288.creator: Mingyang Fu, Yuyang Peng, Dongping Chen, Zetong Zhou, Benlin Liu, Yao Wan, Zhou Zhao, Philip S. Yu, Ranjay Krishna
arxiv-2504-05288.description: Abstract The visual world around us constantly evolves, from real-time news and social media trends to global infrastructure changes visible through satellite imagery and augmented reality enhancements. However, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), which automate many tasks, struggle to stay current, limited by the cutoff dates in their fixed training datasets.

arxiv-2506-22007.title: RoboEnvision: A Long-Horizon Video Generation Model for Multi-Task Robot Manipulation
arxiv-2506-22007.creator: Liudi Yang, Yang Bai, George Eskandar, Fengyi Shen, Mohammad Altillawi, Dong Chen, Soumajit Majumder, Ziyuan Liu, Gitta Kutyniok, Abhinav Valada
arxiv-2506-22007.description: Abstract We address the problem of generating long-horizon videos for robotic manipulation tasks. Text-to-video diffusion models have made significant progress in photorealism, language understanding, and motion generation but struggle with long-horizon robotic tasks. Recent works use video diffusion models for high-quality simulation data and predictive rollouts in robot planning.

pmc-10503510.title: Melatonin Attenuates Sepsis-Induced Acute Lung Injury via Inhibiting Excessive Mitophagy
pmc-10503510.creator: Jianmin Ling, Shanshan Yu, Feng Xiong, Tingting Xu, Shusheng Li
pmc-10503510.description: BackgroundEpidemiological studies have indicated that lung injury is a frequent complication of sepsis. Mitophagy is vital to multiple pathological processes and diseases; however, its influence on sepsis-induced acute lung injury remains elusive. Melatonin has multiple antioxidant action and anti-inflammatory effects, including regulating mitophagy and inflammatory cytokine expression.

pmc-12512749.title: Long-term observation of glare and dynamic pupil after EVO ICL (implantable collamer lens) for myopia
pmc-12512749.creator: Xun Chen, Wuxiao Zhao, Jifang Wang, Mingrui Cheng, Xiaoying Wang, Xingtao Zhou
pmc-12512749.description: PurposeTo investigate the long-term changes in glare and dynamic pupil after EVO ICL implantation in myopic patients and their influencing factors.MethodIn this prospective, consecutive case study, 22 patients (44 eyes, Male/Female = 9/13) underwent EVO-ICL, with a mean age of 25.3 ± 5.4 years and spherical equivalent of -10.52 ± 3.02 D (range: -3.25 D ~ -18.00 D).

pmc-12656753.title: SARS-CoV-2 Serological Surveillance of Both Vaccinated and Unvaccinated Zoo Animals with the Identification of a Sloth Bear and a Tapir with Previous Infection
pmc-12656753.creator: Marie Arvidson, Yashaswi Raj Subedi, Sandipty Kayastha, Angel Mitchell, Kami Alvarado, Xufang Deng, Karen Terio, Matthew Allender, Leyi Wang
pmc-12656753.description: Since its discovery in 2019, SARS-CoV-2 has continued to be detected in both humans and animals worldwide. Currently there is limited research focusing on serological surveillance of wildlife under human care. Here we tested 230 serum samples of 134 animals from two zoological institutions collected between 2015 and 2024.

pmc-13146749.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1836 IDENTIFICATION OF AN IN SILICO-BASED NETWORK PHARMACOLOGY THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY ENHANCING LONG-TERM STROKE RECOVERY
pmc-13146749.creator: Rebecca Szepanowski, Sebastian Vonhof, Jasmin Bahr, Svenja Erkelenz, Stine Mencl, Janine Gronewold, Dirk M Hermann, Jan Baumbach, Christoph Kleinschnitz, Ana Isabel Casas Guijarro
pmc-13146749.description: Background and aimsDespite extensive preclinical work during decades, effective neuroprotective interventions have not yet reached clinical practice. Here, we introduce a systems medicine computational pipeline, designed to identify mechanistically related targets underlying the stroke pathomechanism. We propose a paradigm change evaluating an in silico-based multi-target, network pharmacology intervention in a murine model of focal cerebral ischaemia.

pmc-13323795.title: Two-factor synaptic plasticity enables memory consolidation during neuronal burst firing
pmc-13323795.creator: Kathleen Jacquerie, Danil Tyulmankov, Pierre Sacré, Guillaume Drion
pmc-13323795.description: How can brain circuits remain plastic enough to encode new information while still stabilizing synaptic changes that support long-term memory? Many circuits switch between tonic spiking, which encodes external inputs, and burst firing, which is generated collectively; yet how these firing-state changes interact with synaptic plasticity to support consolidation remains unclear.

pmc-13448700.title: Quality and content evaluation of male HPV infection on Bilibili and TikTok: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13448700.creator: Cheng Wang, Yuling Kou, Huanxin Sun, Zhonghua Li, Wei Kuang
pmc-13448700.description: Social media platforms, particularly short-video applications, have emerged as crucial channels for disseminating public health information. Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in males represents a significant sexually transmitted disease burden with under-addressed health impacts. Despite its prevalence, the quality of HPV-related content targeting male audiences on these platforms remains unevaluated, posing potential risks to public health literacy.

pmc-13522501.creator: Sunghwa Woo, Hyun Gyu Lim, Brenna Norton-Baker, Torrey M. Lind, Nathan E. Gladden, Yan Chen, Ciara de Venecia, Thomas Eng, Christopher W. Johnson, Aindrila Mukhopadhyay, Christopher J. Petzold, Adam M. Guss, Gregg T. Beckham, Adam M. Feist

pmc-13629457.title: Vaccination Reduces Shedding of Salmonid Alphavirus Subtype 3, but Bacterial Co‐Infection Influences the Effect
pmc-13629457.creator: Søren Grove, H. Craig Morton, Dhamotharan Kannimuthu, HyeongJin Roh, Ravikumar M. Chovatia, Ma Michelle Peñaranda, Dawit Ghebretnsae, Kai Ove Skaftnesmo
pmc-13629457.description: Waterborne horizontal transmission of viral diseases in fish relies on the release of infectious virus particles (termed shedding) into the aquatic environment. Both the rate and duration of shedding are critical for efficient viral spread, making interventions that reduce shedding valuable for disease control.
